title: A 12A 89.3% Peak Efficiency and 26mV Undershoot 12-to-1V Two-Stage Converter with Regulated Resonant Switched-Capacitor Regulators
problem: Power converters for data centers and processors require large output current (12A) at sub-1V supply voltages, while achieving high efficiency, low undershoot, and fast transient response across wide voltage ranges (12V to 1V).
motivation: High-performance computing in data centers demands efficient point-of-load (PoL) power delivery with minimal voltage droop and fast settling to support dynamic workloads.
method: Two-stage regulation architecture: an intermediate bus converter (IBC) steps 12V to intermediate voltage with high efficiency, followed by a switched-capacitor point-of-load converter with regulated resonant operation achieving 89.3% peak efficiency and 26mV undershoot.
key_novelty: Integration of regulated resonant switched-capacitor architecture in the low-voltage PoL stage to achieve both high efficiency and fast transient response simultaneously.
contributions: Achieved 89.3% peak efficiency with 12A output capability at sub-1V rails
Two-stage regulation enables efficient 12V-to-1V conversion using CMOS-compatible processes
Improved density and speed compared to single-stage converters
primary_theme: efficient multi-stage power delivery for high-current compute
